notes: D15: sub-millimetre gaps exist only in raw pointer/preview input. Raw values are quantized to integer mm before the command; an endpoint that lands on an existing junction reuses that junction.
Here only quantization + junction reuse are tested (geometry/normalizer, PH0-T02). The full pointer path with pixel snap tolerances is tested in PH2-T03 and must reuse these inputs.

cases.earliestTask: PH0-T02 (quantize + reuse junction); PH2-T03 (full snapping path)
cases.description: Three walls of a 4000 x 3000 rectangle exist. The user closes the loop; the raw pointer end point is 0.4 mm away from the start junction j1.
arithmetic: Both endpoints are existing junctions, so the new wall is j4 -> j1 and no new junction is created (junctionCount stays 4; a duplicate junction at (0,0) would violate I5).
The loop closes: 1 bounded face. Clear: X 100..3900 = 3800, Y 100..2900 = 2800 -> 10,640,000 mm2.
Centreline signed area 4000 x 3000 = 12,000,000 with corners in screen-clockwise order.

cases.description: Same as GAP-01, but the raw end point is 0.6 mm off in X. Quantization gives x = 1, which is 1 mm from j1: NOT merged by I5 (only < 1 mm merges). The model must not silently close on j1; the quantized wall is diagonal, so the command is rejected.
arithmetic: New wall (0,3000) -> (1,0): dx = 1, dy = -3000 -> not axis-aligned -> rejected in L0 (I4). The model is unchanged.
This shows why sub-mm closing must be handled by snapping BEFORE the command (§E.10 priority 1, junction snap), not by the model guessing.
